taxonomyNote: NatureServe uses a narrower concept of D. auriculatus (Means et al. 2017; Pyron et al. 2022), splitting D. valentinei, D. pascagoula and D. valtos from it; Virginia and North Carolina agency pages use the broader concept.
fieldMarks: Brown to black salamander up to about 6.5 in, usually with one or two rows of white side spots.
Belly gray-brown to black with small white speckles.
Laterally compressed tail sharpening toward the tip; a light stripe runs from each eye back to the base of the jaw, as in all dusky salamanders.
behavior: Nocturnal; hides by day under leaves, logs or debris or in burrows.
Opportunistic feeder on arthropods, worms and other invertebrates; Virginia DWR notes cannibalism.
Breeds September-October, 9-20 eggs guarded by the female until fall hatching; larvae are aquatic with external gills and metamorphose the following spring.
habitat: Mucky areas near springs, swamps, cypress heads, mud-bottomed streams, floodplain pools and ravines with organic debris, usually in or near slow water; leaf-litter packs along slow mucky streams in Virginia.
range: Atlantic and Gulf coastal plain: Virginia (to mid Mecklenburg County) and the North Carolina coastal plain per state agencies; NatureServe's narrower concept lists only Alabama and Florida. Not recorded for Canada.
